messages.author: 90b5ae7e2259370d
messages.subject: sort_asc problems
parts:
Hi all,

I've been trying to use sort_asc on part of a 2D array. It works fine(-ish) as long as there are not 'too many' NAN, when I have ~ 13 NAN, it just does not sort anymore (when I index to one element less, it sorts fine). Also, when it sorts, I think it does not sort the NANs consistently - they seem to always appear in a different place in the array (rather than consistently as first or last entries). I'm not sure whether I've coded it wrongly..

Here is the code I used:
real x[A,B]; // array before sorting - I have A=29, B=240
real y[A,B]; // array after sorting

[... code to fill x ...]

for (a in 1:A){
y[a,1:B] <- sort_asc(x[a,1:B]);}

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] sort_asc problems
parts:
Hi Jacquie,

1. I don't think we ever intended for these functions to allow NaN. I believe this is an error in our implementation. I've created an issue for it: https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/253
2. NaN doesn't behave like a number: If x is a real number, both (x < NaN) and (NaN < x) are false. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NaN
3. It's inconsistent due to the underlying implementation relying on std::sort() in C++: http://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/algorithm/sort.

Without the full program, it's hard to tell what you're doing with the NaNs, but you could replace those values with negative_infinity().


Daniel

thanks for the quick reply, this is a great suggestion. The NANs are just there from initialising an array and not filling these values, so putting them as infinity (which I didn't even know existed!) should solve the sorting. 
Thanks!!
